complete_source_units.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, set your face firmly against the sons of Ammon and prophesy against them,

and say to Ammon’s sons, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord: Because you rejoiced over My holy things when they were profaned, over Israel’s land when it was devastated, and over Judah’s house when they went into captivity,

therefore behold, I am handing you to the sons of Kedem as an inheritance. They will camp with their equipment in you and set their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruits and drink your richness.
I will make Ammon’s city pastures for camels, and Ammon’s sons a pasture for sheep. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: Because you clapped your hand and made noise with your foot, and rejoiced from your soul over Israel’s land,

therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’
Thus says the Lord: Because Moab said, ‘Behold, Israel’s and Judah’s house is like all the nations,’
therefore behold, I am paralyzing Moab’s shoulder from its frontier cities, the choice land, the house of Asimouth above a spring of a coastal city.
To Kedem’s sons, against Ammon’s sons, I have given them as an inheritance, so that no remembrance of Ammon’s sons may remain.
I will exact vengeance upon Moab, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: Because Idumea acted in vengeance against Judah’s house, and they bore a grudge and exacted punishment,
therefore thus says the Lord: I will stretch My hand against Idumea and utterly destroy human and animal from her. I will make her a wilderness, and those pursued from Thaiman will fall by the sword.
I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Because the foreigners acted in vengeance and stirred up vengeance, rejoicing from their soul to wipe out for ever,
therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stretch My hand against the foreigners, utterly destroy Cretans and make the remaining inhabitants of the coast perish.
I will execute great acts of vengeance upon them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring My vengeance upon them.”
In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, ‘Well done! She is shattered; the nations have perished. She has turned to me; the full one has been laid waste,’
therefore thus says the Lord: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
They will throw down Tyre’s walls and throw down your towers. I will winnow her dust from her and make her a smooth rock.
She will be a drying place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,
and her daughters in the plain will be killed by the sword. They will know that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: I am bringing against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north—he is king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and an assembly of very many nations.
He will kill your daughters in the plain with the sword, set an advance guard against you, build around you, and make a palisade and a ring of weapons around you; he will set his spears opposite you.
He will throw down your walls and your towers with his swords.

The dust of his multitude of horses will cover you, and your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and his chariots’ wheels when he enters your gates like someone entering a city from the plain.
With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.
He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord, to Tyre: Will not the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and a sword is drawn within you?

All the rulers from the nations of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove the turbans from their heads, and strip off their patterned clothing. They will be utterly astonished, sit on the ground, fear their own destruction, and groan over you.
They will raise a lament over you and say to you: ‘How you were destroyed from the sea, praised city that spread her fear to all who live in her!
The islands will be afraid from the day of your fall.’
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: When I make you a desolated city like cities that will not be inhabited, when I bring the abyss up over you and much water covers you,

I will bring you down to those descending into the pit, to the people of old. I will settle you in the depths of the earth like an everlasting wilderness, with those descending into the pit, so that you are not inhabited and do not rise in the land of life.
I will bring you to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever, says the Lord, the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, take up a lament over Tyre,
and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrance of the sea, the trading place of the peoples from many islands: Thus says the Lord to Tyre: You said, ‘I have clothed myself with my beauty.’
In the heart of the sea, at Beelim, your sons clothed you with beauty.
Cedar from Senir was built for you; strips of cypress planks were taken from Lebanon to make fir masts for you.
From Bashan they made your oars; they made your sacred places from ivory, wooded houses from the islands of Kittim.
Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt became your bedding, to clothe you with glory and wrap you in blue and purple from the islands of Elishah; it became your coverings.
Your rulers who inhabit Sidon, and the Arvadites, became your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, who were in you, were your pilots.
The elders of Byblos and their wise men were in you; they strengthened your counsel. All the ships of the sea and their rowers came to you toward the farthest west.
Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your force; your warrior men hung small shields and helmets in you; they gave you your glory.
Sons of Arvadites and your force were on your walls; guards were in your towers. They hung their quivers around your harbors; they completed your beauty.
Carthaginians were your traders because of the abundance of all your strength; they gave silver, gold, iron, tin, and lead for your market.
Greece, all of it, and the adjoining regions traded with you in human lives, and gave bronze vessels for your commerce.
From the house of Togarmah they gave horses and horsemen for your market.
Sons of Rhodians were your traders; from islands they increased your commerce with ivory tusks, and you gave your payments in exchange for the imported goods,
people as your merchandise from the abundance of your mixed company, myrrh drops and embroideries from Tarshish; Ramoth and Chorchor gave for your market.
Judah and the sons of Israel were your traders in the sale of grain, perfumes, and cassia; they gave choice honey, oil, and resin to your mixed company.
Damascus was your trader because of the abundance of all your strength: wine from Helbon and wool from Miletus;
and they gave wine for your market. From Asel, worked iron and a wheel are among your mixed company.
Dedan was your trader with choice animals for chariots.
Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar were your traders through your hand, with camels, rams, and lambs in which they traded with you.
Traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders with choice spices and good stones, and they gave gold for your market.
Haran and Channa were your traders; Asshur and Charman were your traders,
bringing merchandise, blue cloth and choice treasures bound with cords, and cypress
ships: in them Carthaginians were your traders in abundance among your mixed company. You were filled and became very heavy in the heart of the sea.
Your rowers led you in much water; the south wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.

There were your forces, your payment and that of your mixed companies, your rowers and pilots, your counselors and your mixed companies from your mixed companies, all your warrior men in you, and your whole assembly within you; they will fall in the heart of the sea on the day of your fall.
At the sound of your cry, your pilots will be greatly afraid,
and all your rowers will come down from the ships; the passengers and the lookouts of the sea will stand on the land.
They will raise a cry over you with their voice and cry bitterly; they will put earth on their head and spread ashes beneath them.
Their sons will take up a lament over you and a lamentation for you:
‘What a payment you found from the sea! You filled nations from your abundance, and from your mixed company you enriched all the kings of the earth.
Now you were shattered in the sea, in the depth of water; your mixed company and all your assembly fell within you—all your rowers.
All who inhabit the islands became gloomy over you; their kings were utterly astonished, and their faces shed tears.
Traders from nations hissed at you; you came to ruin, and you will be no more for ever.’”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord: Because your heart was exalted and you said, ‘I am a god; I have inhabited a god’s dwelling in the heart of the sea’—yet you are a human, and not a god, and you made your heart like a god’s heart—
Surely you are not wiser than Daniel? Did wise men not instruct you in their knowledge?
Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?
By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you made your heart like a god’s heart,

therefore, behold, I am bringing foreigners against you, scourges from nations. They will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your knowledge, and lay your beauty out for destruction,
and they will bring you down; you will die the death of wounded men in the heart of the sea.
Surely you will not say, ‘I am a god,’ before those killing you? You are a human, and not a god. In a multitude
of uncircumcised people you will perish by foreigners’ hands, for I have spoken, says the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: You were a seal of likeness and a crown of beauty;

you came to be in the delight of God’s paradise. You have been clothed with every good stone: carnelian, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, jasper, silver, gold, ligurite, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. You filled your treasuries and storehouses within you with gold from the day you were created.
With the cherub I placed you on God’s holy mountain; you came to be among fiery stones.
You were blameless in your days from the day you were created until wrongdoings were found in you.
From the abundance of your trade you filled your store chambers with lawlessness, and you sinned and were wounded away from God’s mountain; the cherub led you out from among fiery stones.

Your heart was exalted because of your beauty; your knowledge was corrupted together with your beauty. Because of your many sins I threw you to the ground; I placed you before kings to be made a spectacle.

Because of your many sins and the wrongdoings of your trade you profaned your sacred places. I will bring fire out from within you; it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on your land before all who see you.
All who know you among the nations will become gloomy over you; you came to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, fix your face upon Sidon and prophesy against her,
and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. You will know that I am the Lord when I execute judgments in you, and I will be sanctified in you.
Blood and death will be in your broad streets, and wounded men will fall by swords in you, all around you. They will know that I am the Lord.
The house of Israel will no longer have a thorn of bitterness or a thorn of pain from all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will gather Israel from the nations where they were scattered, and I will be sanctified in them before the peoples and the nations. They will dwell on their land, which I have given to My servant Jacob,

and they will dwell on it in hope, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell in hope when I execute judgment on all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.”
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, fix your face upon Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt,
and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh, the great dragon seated among his rivers, who says, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’
I will put traps in your jaws and fasten the fish of your river to your fins. I will bring you up from the midst of your river, and all the fish of your river,

and I will cast you down quickly, and all the fish of your river. You will fall on the face of the plain; you will certainly not be gathered or wrapped for burial. I have given you for food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven.
All who inhabit Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you became a reed staff for the house of Israel.
When they took hold of you with their hand, you were crushed; and when every hand prevailed against them, and when they rested upon you, you were shattered and broke all their loins.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy humans and livestock from you.
The land of Egypt will become a ruin and a wilderness, and they will know that I am the Lord, because you say, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’
Therefore, behold, I am against you and against all your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt a wilderness, a sword, and destruction, from Migdol and Syene as far as the borders of the Ethiopians.
No human foot will pass through it, nor will livestock’s foot pass through it; it will not be inhabited for forty years.
I will make her land a ruin amid desolated land, and her cities will be amid desolated cities for forty years. I will scatter Egypt among the nations and winnow them into the countries.
Thus says the Lord: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations where they were scattered,
and I will turn back the captivity of the Egyptians and settle them in the land of Pathros, in the land from which they were taken; it will be a lowly dominion
among all the dominions; it will no longer be exalted over the nations, and I will make them few, so that they are not more numerous among the nations.
They will no longer be a hope for the house of Israel, bringing lawlessness to remembrance when they follow after them. They will know that I am the Lord.”
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first of the first month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his force to great servitude against Tyre; every head was bald and every shoulder was losing its hair. Yet neither he nor his force received wages for Tyre and the servitude they performed against her.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take her booty and strip her spoils; it will be wages for his force.
In exchange for his service, which he performed against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
On that day a horn will spring up for the whole house of Israel, and I will give you an opened mouth among them. They will know that I am the Lord.”
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: Alas, alas, the day!
For the Lord’s day is near; it will be a day, an end of nations.
A sword will come upon the Egyptians, and there will be turmoil in Ethiopia; wounded men will fall in Egypt, and her foundations will collapse together.
Persians, Cretans, Lydians, Libyans, all the mixed company, and some of the sons of My covenant will fall by the sword in her.
Egypt’s supports will fall, and the arrogance of her strength will come down from Migdol to Syene; they will fall in her by the sword, says the Lord.
She will be desolated among desolated countries, and their cities will be among desolated cities.
They will know that I am the Lord when I put fire upon Egypt and all who help her are shattered.
On that day messengers will go out, hastening to lay Ethiopia waste; turmoil will be among them on Egypt’s day, for behold, it is coming.
Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the multitude of Egyptians by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,
him and his people: scourges from nations sent to destroy the land. They will all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land will be filled with wounded men.
I will make their rivers desolate and destroy the land and all that fills it by foreigners’ hands. I, the Lord, have spoken.
For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the magnates from Memphis and the rulers from the land of Egypt, and they will be no more.
I will destroy the land of Pathros, put fire upon Tanis, and execute vengeance in Diospolis,
and pour out My wrath upon Sais, Egypt’s strength, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.
I will put fire upon Egypt; Syene will be greatly troubled, and in Diospolis there will be a breach, and waters will pour out.
The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.
At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I shatter Egypt’s scepters there and the arrogance of her strength perishes there. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will be led away captive.
I will execute judgment in Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, I shattered the arms of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Behold, it has not been bound up to provide healing, to put a poultice upon it, to give strength to grasp a sword.
Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will shatter his arms, the strong and the outstretched, and cast his sword down from his hand,
and scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword into his hand; he will bring it upon Egypt, take her booty, and strip her spoils.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall. They will know that I am the Lord when I put My sword into the hands of the king of Babylon and he stretches it over the land of Egypt.
I will scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries. All will know that I am the Lord.”
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, say to Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and to his multitude, ‘To whom did you liken yourself in your height?
Behold, Assyria was a cypress in Lebanon, beautiful in offshoots and tall in size; its crown reached into the midst of clouds.
Water nourished it; the abyss raised it high, led its rivers around its plantings and sent out its gatherings of water to all the plain’s trees.
Therefore its size rose above all the plain’s trees, and its branches spread wide because of abundant water.
All the sky’s birds nested in its offshoots; all the plain’s beasts gave birth beneath its branches, and every multitude of nations lived in its shade.
It was beautiful in its height because of the multitude of its branches, for its roots reached abundant water.
Such cypresses did not exist in God’s paradise; pines were not like its offshoots, and firs were not like its branches. No tree in God’s paradise resembled it in its beauty
because of the multitude of its branches, and the trees of God’s paradise of delight envied it.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you became great in size and set your crown amid clouds, and I saw it being lifted high,
I handed it into the hands of a ruler of nations, and he brought about its destruction.

Foreigners, scourges from nations, utterly destroyed it and cast it upon the mountains. Its branches fell in all the ravines; its trunks were shattered in every plain of the land. All the nations’ peoples went down from their shelter and dashed it to the ground.
All the sky’s birds rested upon its fallen trunk, and all the field’s beasts were upon its trunks,

so that none of the trees in the water may rise high in their size. They did not set their crowns amid clouds, and none of those drinking water stood toward them in their height. All were given to death, to the depth of the earth, among human beings, with those descending to a pit.

Thus says the Lord, the Lord: On the day it descended to Hades, the abyss mourned it. I stopped its rivers and restrained the multitude of water. Lebanon grew dark over it, and all the plain’s trees collapsed over it.

At the sound of its fall the nations shook when I brought it down to Hades with those descending to a pit. In the earth all the trees of delight and the choice trees of Lebanon, all drinking water, comforted it.
For they too went down with it to Hades among those wounded by the sword; its offspring, those living under its shelter, perished in the midst of their life.

Whom were you likened to? Descend and be brought down with the trees of delight into the earth’s depth. Among the uncircumcised you will lie with those wounded by the sword. So it is with Pharaoh and the multitude of his strength, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
In the eleventh year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and say to him, ‘You were likened to a lion of nations, and you are like the dragon in the sea. You butted in your rivers, troubled water with your feet and trampled your rivers.
Thus says the Lord: I will throw nets of many peoples over you and haul you up with My hook,
and stretch you out upon the earth; plains will be filled with you. I will seat all the sky’s birds upon you and fill all the beasts of the whole earth with you.
I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill them with your blood,
and the earth will be watered from your discharges, from your multitude upon the mountains. I will fill ravines with you.
When you are extinguished, I will cover heaven and darken its stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon certainly will not show its light.
All the things shining light in heaven will grow dark over you, and I will put darkness upon your land, says the Lord, the Lord.
I will provoke the heart of many peoples when I bring your captivity among the nations, into a land you have not known.
Many nations will grow gloomy over you; their kings will be utterly astounded when My sword flies before their faces, awaiting their own fall from the day of your fall.
For thus says the Lord: Babylon’s king’s sword will come upon you
with giants’ swords, and I will strike down your strength. All are scourges from nations; they will destroy Egypt’s arrogance, and all her strength will be shattered.
I will destroy all her livestock beside the abundant water. No human foot will ever trouble it again, nor will livestock’s tread trample it.
Thus their waters will then become still, and their rivers will flow like oil, says the Lord.
When I give Egypt to destruction and the land is made desolate with its fullness, when I scatter all who dwell in her, they will know that I am the Lord.
It is a lament, and you will lament it, and the nations’ daughters will lament it. Over Egypt and all her strength they will lament her, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
In the twelfth year, in the first month, on the fifteenth of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, lament over Egypt’s strength. The nations will bring her daughters down dead into the earth’s depth, with those descending to a pit.
They will fall with him among those wounded by the sword, and all his strength will lie down.
The giants will say to you, ‘Be in the depth of a pit! Whom do you surpass? Descend and lie with the uncircumcised among those wounded by the sword.’
There Assyria and all his assembly, all wounded, were placed. Their burial is in the depth of a pit, and his assembly was around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword,
who spread their fear upon the land of life.

There is Elam and all his force around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword and those descending uncircumcised into the earth’s depth, who spread their fear upon the land of life and received their torment with those descending to a pit,
among the wounded.
There were placed Mosoch and Thobel and all their strength around his tomb, all his wounded, all uncircumcised, wounded by the sword, who spread their fear upon the land of life.

They lay with the giants who fell long ago, who descended to Hades with weapons of war and put their swords beneath their heads. Their lawless deeds were upon their bones, because they terrified giants in the land of life.
You too will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword.
There were placed Assyria’s rulers, who gave his strength to a sword wound. These lay with the wounded, with those descending to a pit.

There are the north’s rulers, all Assyria’s generals, who descended wounded. With their fear and their strength they lay uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword and carried away their torment with those descending to a pit.
King Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all their strength, says the Lord, the Lord.
For I have set his fear upon the land of life, and he will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitude—says the Lord, the Lord.”
